subject: Electrical Engineering
title: The MOSFET: Voltage Controls Current
description: A 60-second lesson on The MOSFET: Voltage Controls Current.

hook.text: Apply a voltage to the gate and a channel opens between source and drain. No current flows into the gate.

buildup.text: A thin oxide insulates the gate from the channel. The electric field does all the work.

discovery.text: MOSFETs draw almost zero gate current. They switch faster and waste less power than BJTs.

twist.text: CMOS pairs N-channel and P-channel MOSFETs so one is always off — near-zero idle power.

climax.text: Every modern processor contains billions of MOSFETs — all switching with voltage, not current.

punchline.text: A voltage whisper opens the gate. No current needed — just a field.

quiz.question: What advantage do MOSFETs have over bipolar transistors?
options: They draw almost zero gate current, saving energy
They are easier to manufacture from germanium
